text: When an ECP5 FIR is DSP-capped at 12>8 while timing has margin (235.7 MHz, 4.24 ns carry-chain accumulator), do not apply symmetric fold=2 with dsp_regs=in_pipe_out without checking the pre-multiplier path: it reaches 8 DSP but Fmax falls to 100.7 MHz because the 2:1 operand mux/coefficient ROM makes FF part[1] -> LUT4 out_data -> carry-chain the 9.93 ns critical path.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR meets its 8-DSP cap at fold=2 but is timing-limited by the post-multiplier gather into a 36-cell carry chain over 4.33 ns of route, insert two fabric pipeline stages after the multiplier (pipe_mul 0→2) to split the accumulation path, gaining +11.2 MHz (100.7→111.9 MHz) for +2 LUT and 0 DSP.

When an ECP5 symmetric-folded FIR with 8 DSPs is timing-limited at 111.9 MHz by a fabric path of part[0] FF → 6-LUT4 out_data tree → 34-cell carry chain, avoid changing acc_width 40→38, pipe_mul 2→3, and reg_in false→true: it cut LUTs by 43 but dropped Fmax 6.4 MHz to 105.5 MHz with no DSP savings and remained infeasible because the accumulator/fabric sum, not the multiplier pipeline, dominates.

When a symmetric folded FIR on ECP5 is timing-limited by routing through the tap-operand mux/coefficient ROM (critical path FF -> 5-cell LUT4 (~4.2 ns route) -> 33-cell carry chain, no DSP), increase fold from 2 to 4 (halving DSPs from 8 to 4) to relieve pre-multiplier congestion, which shortens the carry chain to 9 cells and raises Fmax by 24.3 MHz (105.5 to 129.8 MHz) while cutting 457 LUTs.

When the ECP5 4-fold symmetric FIR hits 129.8 MHz on the 17-bit pre-adder carry chain (2.29 ns) into the MULT18X18D A input, de-share the coefficients and double fold to 8 to keep 4 MACs/4 DSPs and cut the pre-adder, but the replacement 3-level 8:1 operand mux becomes critical, so LUTs fall 137 while Fmax drops 3.5 MHz to 126.3 MHz—fix the mux or leave the pre-adder.

When an ECP5 FIR is DSP-infeasible at 12 DSP and 235.7 MHz with the 40-bit accumulator carry chain as the critical path, switch to symmetric fold=4 with explicit pipelined MULT18X18D to reach 4 DSP, accepting 125.8 MHz (-109.9 MHz) because the 4:1 tap-operand mux/coefficient ROM and 17-bit symmetric pre-adder into the DSP A input become the limiter.

When an ECP5 FIR is timing-rich at 236 MHz but violates a 6-DSP budget with 12 MULT18X18D and dsp_regs=none, use symmetric fold=4 with reg_in and in_pipe_out and acc_width=38 to reach 4 DSPs and 963 LUTs, but expect Fmax to fall to 129 MHz (-107 MHz) because the 4:1 tap/pre-adder carry chain into the MULT18X18D A input becomes the 7.75 ns critical path instead of the 4.23 ns accumulator.

When an ECP5 transposed FIR is already feasible at the 1-sample/cycle throughput bound with spare timing margin and the accumulator carry chain on sum_r[0] is both the critical path and LUT hotspot, trim the accumulator from 32 to its legal 28-bit minimum (12+12+ceil(log2 16)) to shorten the carry chain from 29 to 24 cells, cutting 40 LUTs and lifting Fmax from 257.3 to 272.5 MHz with no DSP or throughput cost.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is feasible but routing-limited on the 17-bit pre-adder/tap-operand path into the DSP A port (7.75 ns: x_d FF -> 14-cell carry -> LUT4 -> MULT18X18D), trim acc_width 40 -> 38 and drop pipe_mul 1 -> 0 because the DSP's in_pipe_out already registers P, gaining 0.5 MHz (129.0 -> 129.6) and cutting 18 LUTs by relieving operand-mux routing (1.09 -> 0.63 ns) without changing the 4 DSPs or 1/4 throughput.

When a folded symmetric FIR on ECP5 is feasible at 129.6 MHz but timing-limited by the 14-cell pre-adder carry chain feeding the MULT18X18D A port, avoid enabling pipe_mul=1—it adds a fabric register after the DSP output without touching that path, dropping Fmax 0.9 MHz to 128.7 with no LUT/DSP change—and instead cut the pre-adder/accumulator gather (e.g. reduce accumulator width).

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is feasible but critical path is the 11-16-cell pre-adder/tap-operand carry chain into the MULT18X18D A port, do not add a fabric multiplier pipeline stage (pipe_mul=1 to 2), since it only moves 128.7 to 131.5 MHz (+2.8 MHz) with 0 LUT/DSP change and leaves the same carry-chain path critical because the bottleneck is operand gathering before the DSP, not the post-multiplier register.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is already feasible at 129 MHz with 4 DSPs but timing-limited by the pre-multiplier carry-chain/LUT route into the MULT18X18D A input, cut acc_width 40→38 and raise pipe_mul 1→2: this gave +2.5 MHz (131.5 MHz), -18 LUT, and unchanged 4 DSP, with the critical path shifting to a shorter 11-cell carry chain (7.6 ns) rather than removing the operand-path bottleneck.

On ECP5 folded symmetric FIR, when the feasible 131.5 MHz design is timing-limited by the input-FF→pre-adder carry/LUT route into MULT18X18D, do not strip the multiplier pipeline (pipe_mul 2→0): it leaves LUT/DSP unchanged but drops Fmax 1.9 MHz to 129.6 MHz because the critical pre-multiply path only lengthens from 7.60 to 7.72 ns.

On an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR that is feasible at 129.6 MHz with the critical path running through the multiplier-operand carry chain into MULT18X18D A, skip pipe_mul=1 because enabling it drops Fmax to 128.7 MHz (-0.9) with unchanged 965 LUTs/4 DSPs and no relief on that operand path.

For an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR with a critical path running input register -> pre-adder carry chain -> operand mux -> DSP A, removing the input register and setting pipe_mul=2 gives only +3.8 MHz (128.7 to 132.5 MHz) because the 0.52 ns saved at the register is negligible against the ~3.8 ns of carry-chain logic and routing, so target the pre-adder or mux instead.

On an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR whose ~132 MHz critical path is the pre-adder carry chain into the MULT18X18D A input, don't expect swapping the DSP register from in_pipe_out to in_out to fix timing: it gives only +2.8 MHz (132.5→135.3 MHz) for +1 LUT and the same 4 DSP because it removes an internal pipeline stage while leaving the pre-adder-to-A-input bottleneck intact.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is timing-limited by the routing-dominated pre-adder carry chain into the MULT18X18D A input (7.39 ns), do not increase fabric pipeline depth after the multiplier (pipe_mul 2→3) to chase Fmax: it left 965 LUT/4 DSP unchanged and dropped Fmax 135.3→129.5 MHz, because registers after the multiplier cannot cut the pre-adder-to-DSP-A path.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is DSP-bound with the critical path through the pre-adder carry chain, avoid combining pipe_mul 3→2, reg_in true→false, and dsp_regs in_pipe_out→in_out for a 1-LUT saving because Fmax drops 1.6 MHz (129.5→127.9) as the path shifts to a longer carry-chain/LUT route (7.72→7.82 ns), so keep reg_in=true and in_pipe_out unless LUT is the binding constraint.

On ECP5, when a folded symmetric FIR at 127.9 MHz is carry-chain-limited in the pre-adder before a MULT18X18D and already uses the minimum 4 DSPs/964 LUTs, do not switch dsp_regs to in_out+out, as it lengthened that carry-chain-to-LUT path from 7.82 ns/8 cells to 11.0 ns/13 cells and cut Fmax by 37 MHz to 90.9 MHz with zero LUT/DSP savings (lost feasibility).

When a folded symmetric FIR on ECP5 is feasible at ~133 MHz with 4 DSP/983 LUT and the critical path is a multiplier carry chain, shrink acc_width from 40 to the legal 38 bits (16+16+log2(32)+1) to cut 18 LUTs and gain ~1.7 MHz to ~134.6 MHz with unchanged DSP.

On an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR whose feasible timing is limited by the g_mac tap-operand carry chain, do not delete the fabric post-multiplier pipeline just because the DSP P register is already enabled: pipe_mul 2→0 left 965 LUT and 4 DSP unchanged but dropped Fmax 134.6→129.9 MHz (−4.8 MHz) while the critical path merely moved between g_mac carry chains (7.43→7.70 ns).

On an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR whose critical path is the MULT18X18D tap-operand carry chain, do not move the input and M→P pipeline registers inside the DSP (in_out→in_pipe_out) to buy timing, since it dropped Fmax 129.87→128.21 MHz and added 1 LUT at the same 4 DSP because the carry chain, not the register placement, remained the bottleneck.

When a folded symmetric FIR on ECP5 is timing-limited at 164.4 MHz by a 21-cell carry-chain final reduction of M=4 partial sums (FF part[1] through out_data LUTs), enable the registered balanced sum tree, adding 2 cycles of latency to cut that chain and reach 219.0 MHz (+54.6 MHz) with 70 fewer LUTs and no extra DSPs.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is timing-limited by the g_mac[*].u_m.a_ext carry chain (2 cells, 0.89+1.47 ns of 4.57 ns), don't re-pipeline the DSP registers to in_pipe_out/in_out: it only moved the critical path to g_mac[3] (5 cells, 0.96+1.46 ns) and reduced Fmax 219.0→216.5 MHz (−2.5 MHz) with LUT/DSP unchanged (445/4), because a_ext operand-extension logic sits outside the DSP register stages being changed.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is DSP-cap-limited and timing-limited by the post-accumulator reduction carry chain, do not switch dsp_regs from in_out to in_pipe_out or drop pipe_in to save operand-mux registers, because it moves the critical path to the multiplier A7 carry chain and drops Fmax from 216.5 to 149.2 MHz (-67.3 MHz) with no LUT/DSP savings, making the design infeasible.

On an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR at fold=2/4 DSP whose Fmax is limited by a 13-cell carry chain feeding a DSP operand, enable both pipe_in and sum_tree: pipe_in splits the DSP-operand path and the registered tree removes the M=4 combinational partial-sum chain, yielding +8.1 MHz (151.8→159.9 MHz) and −70 LUTs at unchanged 4 DSPs, though the accumulator carry chain becomes the new limiter and 200 MHz is still missed.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is timing-limited by a MULT18X18D feeding a 28-cell 29-bit accumulator carry chain at fold=2/4 DSP, switch to fold=4 with pipe_mul=1 to halve DSPs 4->2 and LUTs 445->407, move the critical path to a 6-cell a_ext carry chain, and lift Fmax 159.9->188.5 MHz because fewer fixed DSP source sites load the accumulator and the multiplier output is registered.

When an ECP5 symmetric folded FIR misses timing at 188.5 MHz because the critical path is the x_d→6-cell pre-adder carry chain→4:1 tap-operand LUT4 into the multiplier rather than the accumulator, de-share coefficients (symmetric false, fold=4), drop acc_width 29→28, and add multiplier pipelining pipe_mul 1→2, which removes the pre-adder from the path and cuts it to 4.54 ns, raising Fmax to 220.5 MHz (+32 MHz) at 4 DSPs and 385 LUTs.

When an ECP5 FIR is DSP-capped at 12 DSP against a 6-DSP budget while timing-feasible at 236 MHz via a 4.23 ns carry-chain accumulator, symmetric-fold to fold=4 with a 38-bit accumulator, input/DSP output registers, pipe_in, and a registered balanced sum tree to cut to 4 DSP and 904 LUT and become feasible, but expect Fmax to drop to 164.7 MHz because the 36-cell accumulator carry chain (2.06 ns logic + 2.57 ns route) becomes the 6.07 ns critical path, so pipeline that accumulator next.

Do not add a sum tree to an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR that is already feasible at 164.7 MHz with the accumulator carry chain critical at 6.07 ns: it adds 54 LUTs and no DSPs, moves the critical path to a 16-cell out_data carry chain at 6.65 ns, and drops Fmax to 150.3 MHz.

On an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR routing-limited by the out_data carry-chain accumulator, enabling pipe_in shifts the critical path to the MULT18X18D operand carry chain (u_mult_A4) and drops Fmax by 21.3 MHz (150.3→129.0) for +5 LUTs, so leave pipe_in disabled unless you also pipeline the operand path.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR with 4 DSPs is routing-limited on the post-multiply MULT18X18D-to-accumulator carry path (7.75 ns / 129 MHz), add a second fabric pipeline stage after the multiplier (pipe_mul=2) with input and sum-tree pipelining to isolate that cross-column route, yielding 176 MHz (+47 MHz) and 59 fewer LUTs at unchanged 4 DSPs.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is carry-chain-bound at ~176 MHz on the DSP-output-to-accumulator path, do not insert a fabric register between MULT18X18D and the accumulator (pipe_mul) expecting a speedup: it gave 175.96 MHz (-0.2 MHz) with LUT=904/DSP=4 unchanged because the removed DSP-to-CARRY route reappeared as a 1.94 ns LUT route while the carry chain shrank from 16 to 3 cells.

When a transposed ECP5 FIR is infeasible only on DSP count (16 MULT18X18D vs a 6-DSP budget) while timing has margin (220.5 MHz, critical path the 38-cell sum_r carry-chain), fold by 4 with a 38-bit accumulator and enable DSP input/output registers plus a registered balanced sum tree, trading 44 MHz (220.5→176.5 MHz, still clearing 120 MHz) for 16→4 DSP and 1340→904 LUT, because the resulting 4:1 tap-operand mux/pre-adder ahead of the DSP A input becomes the critical path and must be pipelined.

On an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR (U=16, fold=4, 4 DSPs), when the carry-chain accumulator is the limiter, do not remove the input pipeline register (pipe_in true→false): it exposes the x_d→pre-adder/tap-mux carry-chain path, increasing the critical path from 5.67 to 7.28 ns and cutting Fmax from 176.5 to 137.4 MHz (−39.1 MHz) for +7 LUTs and no DSP reduction.

On an ECP5 4-DSP folded symmetric FIR with the multiplier operand mux/pre-adder on the 7.28 ns critical path, enable the sum tree, set pipe_mul=1, and disable pipe_in to gain +14.2 MHz (137.4→151.6 MHz) at +47 LUT and no DSP change, shifting the critical path to the 32-cell out_data carry chain.

When an ECP5 FIR is DSP-budget-limited at 12 MULT18X18D with a slack 4.23 ns carry-chain path, switch to symmetric fold=4 with pipelined in/out DSP registers and a sum tree to cut to 4 DSP and 904 LUT, accepting Fmax falling from 236 to 165 MHz because the new 36-cell accumulator carry chain becomes the 6.07 ns critical path.

On an ECP5 DSP-registered folded symmetric FIR already feasible at 164.7 MHz with the accumulator carry chain critical, do not add a balanced sum-tree output, since it costs 54 LUTs and drops Fmax to 150.3 MHz by shifting the critical path to the out_data carry chain (1.35+1.63 ns).

On ECP5 folded symmetric FIR, when fold=4 meets timing but burns 4 DSPs, move to fold=8 with a balanced sum tree—it halves DSPs (4→2) and cuts LUTs 958→867 for only 4.9 MHz Fmax loss (150.3→145.4 MHz), because the smaller 2:1 tap mux shortens the a_ext carry chain to 6 cells and leaves the path routing-limited rather than carry-limited.
